config.title: Design DataTable API

intro.title: Design DataTable API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will design a reusable DataTable API in Angular to display structured data. You will learn how to define a TypeScript interface that specifies the shape and properties of the data table, such as columns and rows. The core concept involves using Angular's component-based architecture and TypeScript interfaces to create a clear, type-safe API. By the end, you'll have a foundational understanding of how to structure data-driven components for consistent use across your application.
intro.usecase: DataTable APIs are essential for building enterprise dashboards and admin panels where users need to sort, filter, and paginate through large datasets. In e-commerce platforms, product management interfaces use DataTables to display inventory with column sorting and search capabilities. Financial applications rely on DataTable APIs to present transaction histories with customizable columns and export functionality. Developers implement these APIs to create reusable, consistent data presentation layers across customer relationship management (CRM) systems and analytics tools.

objectives: Implement a DataTable component with configurable column definitions
Apply TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of table data and columns
Construct a service to fetch and manage data for the DataTable
Configure input properties to control table behavior and appearance
Bind dynamic data to the table template for real-time rendering
Integrate sorting and filtering logic into the DataTable API
Initialize and manipulate pagination controls within the DataTable

steps.title: Import Angular core modules and define DataTable interface
steps.instruction: Import Component and Input from '@angular/core' and define an interface named DataTable with columns and data properties.
steps.hint: Use the import statement for Component and Input, then create an interface with properties: columns (array of strings) and data (array of objects).
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component and Input from '@angular/core'
// Define the DataTable interface with columns and data properties
steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have the necessary imports and a DataTable interface ready for use in the component.
successCriteria: Component and Input are imported from '@angular/core', and a DataTable interface is defined with columns: string[] and data: any[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both imports and the interface are correctly defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported Component and Input and defined the DataTable interface with the required properties.

steps.title: Create DataTable component with basic structure
steps.instruction: Create the DataTableComponent class with the @Component decorator, a selector of 'app-data-table', and an empty template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. The selector should be a custom HTML tag name, and the template can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableComponent class is created with the @Component decorator, a selector, and an empty template.
successCriteria: DataTableComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector set to 'app-data-table', and template property set to an empty string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, and the class is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector and template properties, and the class is properly defined.

steps.title: Add Input properties for columns configuration
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTableComponent class, add an @Input() property called columns with type Array<{key: string, label: string}>.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator before the property declaration. Remember to specify the type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableComponent will have a typed columns input property ready to receive configuration data.
successCriteria: The DataTableComponent class contains an @Input() property named columns with type Array<{key: string, label: string}>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you used the @Input() decorator and specified the correct type for the columns property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The columns input property is missing or incorrect. Check that you used @Input() and the proper type annotation.

steps.title: Add Input property for data rows
steps.instruction: In the DataTableComponent class, add an @Input() property called 'data' with type 'any[]' to hold the table rows.
steps.hint: Use the @Input() decorator before the property declaration, similar to how you added the columns property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableComponent now has two input properties: columns for configuration and data for the table rows.
successCriteria: The DataTableComponent class contains an @Input() property named 'data' with type 'any[]'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the @Input() decorator and specified the type as 'any[]'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data input property is missing or incorrect. Check that you've used @Input() and declared it as 'data: any[]'.

steps.title: Create the table structure in template
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTableComponent's @Component decorator, replace the empty template string with a basic HTML table structure containing <table>, <thead>, and <tbody> elements.
steps.hint: The template should be a string with HTML table markup. Start with '<table>', then add '<thead>' and '<tbody>' sections inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a basic HTML table structure with table, thead, and tbody elements.
successCriteria: The template property in @Component decorator contains a string with '<table>', '<thead>', and '<tbody>' tags.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your template includes all three required elements: <table>, <thead>, and <tbody>.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the empty template string with a complete HTML table structure containing table, thead, and tbody elements.

steps.title: Render table headers dynamically from columns
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTableComponent template, add a <thead> element containing a <tr> with <th> elements that use *ngFor to iterate through the columns array and display each column name.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngFor directive to loop through the columns array and create a table header cell for each item.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: using *ngFor to render list items
  • {{ item }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTableComponent template will contain a <thead> with dynamically generated <th> elements based on the columns input property.
successCriteria: The template includes <thead> with <tr> and <th> elements using *ngFor="let column of columns" to display each column.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have <thead> containing <tr> with <th> elements that use *ngFor to iterate through columns.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required structure. Review how to use *ngFor to create table headers dynamically.

steps.title: Render table rows dynamically from data
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a <tbody> element with an *ngFor directive to loop through the data array and create table rows. For each row, create <td> elements for each column using another *ngFor loop.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let row of data" on the <tr> element, then inside it use *ngFor="let column of columns" on <td> elements to display row[column].
steps.analogousExample: // Example: nested loops in Angular template {{ item[field] }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a <tbody> with dynamic rows and cells that display data values based on the columns configuration.
successCriteria: Nested *ngFor loop iterates over columns array
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have both *ngFor loops correctly structured and that cell content displays the actual data values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table rows aren't rendering dynamically yet. Make sure to add the <tbody> with *ngFor loops for both data rows and column cells.

steps.title: Display cell data using column keys
steps.instruction: In your template, inside the <td> element, use bracket notation to display the data for each cell: {{ row[column] }}
steps.hint: Angular's interpolation {{ }} can access object properties dynamically. For each row and column, you need to display the value at row[column].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: accessing object property dynamically in template
{{ user[propertyName] }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The table will display actual data values in each cell instead of empty cells.
successCriteria: Each <td> element contains {{ row[column] }} to display the corresponding data value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the correct syntax: {{ row[column] }} inside each <td> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table cells are still empty. Remember to use bracket notation with interpolation: {{ row[column] }} to access the data dynamically.

steps.title: Add sorting functionality to column headers
steps.instruction: In the DataTableComponent class, add a sortColumn method that takes a column parameter and sorts the data array based on that column.
steps.hint: Define a method sortColumn(column: string) that sorts the data array in place using the sort method and the column value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a sortColumn method that can sort the data array by a given column.
successCriteria: The DataTableComponent class contains a sortColumn method that accepts a column parameter and sorts the data array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but make sure it's named sortColumn and takes a column parameter to sort the data array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sortColumn method is missing or incorrectly implemented. Add a method that sorts the data array based on a column parameter.

steps.title: Add sorting indicator in template
steps.instruction: Add sorting indicator arrows (↑/↓) next to column headers in your template to show visual feedback for the current sort direction.
steps.hint: Use a conditional expression with *ngIf to show either an up arrow or down arrow based on the sort direction. You'll need to track which column is being sorted and the direction.
steps.expectedOutcome: Column headers will display sorting arrows (↑ for ascending, ↓ for descending) when sorted, providing clear visual feedback to users.
successCriteria: The template includes sorting indicator arrows next to column headers using conditional rendering with *ngIf based on sort state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the sorting indicators might not be displaying correctly. Make sure you're using *ngIf to conditionally show the appropriate arrow based on sort direction.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sorting indicators aren't implemented yet. Remember to add arrow symbols (↑/↓) next to column headers and use conditional rendering to show them based on the current sort state.
